title: Compatibility-fade and Proactive Upgrade Concierge playbook
creator: Priya Narayanan
description: Goal: Create an end-to-end playbook that operationalizes a staged compatibility degradation ("fade") for legacy API behavior and model variants while offering a proactive upgrade concierge for high-usage customers. This playbook should minimize customer downtime, reduce support load, and provide clear migration paths and automated tooling to accelerate upgrades. It will be used as the source of truth for the PM, Console, Docs, SDK, Developer Relations, Support, and Sales teams during the rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Playbook document approved by PM, Eng lead, Docs, and Support lead
Console banners and in-product upgrade CTA implemented in staging
Automated migration checklist template available for Customer Success (CSV + linkable steps)
Release notes and in-product changelog prepared and validated for accessibility and localization
Telemetry hooks defined so we can measure upgrade conversion rate, errors-on-upgrade, and post-upgrade regressions
tasks: Draft high-level migration pathways (automatic, assisted, manual) with rollback guidance
Define deprecation windows and phased capability reductions (alpha, soft-deprecate, hard-deprecate)
Create in-product communications: banners, modal flows, and acknowledgement audit for enterprise tenants
Prepare SDK warnings and compile-time/runtime deprecation notices across Python/Node/Go
Coordinate release-note copy and in-console changelog entries with Docs
Enable telemetry events (migration_started, migration_completed, migration_failed, migration_skipped) in runtime
Design customer segmentation for tiered outreach (high-usage, security-sensitive, self-serve) for Concierge team
Create support playbook for CSEs: runbooks, escalation matrix, pre-approved workarounds
communications_plan: T-60 days: Publish detailed migration guide on docs.redwood.ai and add FAQ; notify active customers via email digest
T-45 days: Open FAQ AMA with Developer Relations and post community forum topic; post migration checklist in support portal
T-30 days: In-product banner appears for all applicable customers linking to guided migration and scheduling concierge call
T-14 days: Targeted outreach from CSMs to top 50 affected accounts; Sales notified with talk tracks
T-0 day: Begin soft-deprecation window; release notes and console banner show exact limits
T+30 days: Hard-deprecation for default routing; customers with active concierge exceptions will have extended window
rollout_timeline: Phase 0 (Prep, weeks 0-4): Finalize playbook, implement telemetry, staging QA for console UX
Phase 1 (Awareness, weeks 5-8): Docs release, community AMA, first emails
Phase 2 (Guided Migration, weeks 9-12): Concierge scheduling, in-product CTAs, automated upgrade tools enabled
Phase 3 (Soft-deprecate, weeks 13-16): Reduced compatibility behavior behind flags, monitoring for errors
Phase 4 (Hard-deprecate, week 17): Remove legacy behavior for non-exempt tenants, escalate failures to on-call as needed
stakeholders: Engineering: Rafael Sousa (Runtime lead), Mei Lin (SDK lead)
linked_artifacts: GitHub PRs: runtime: refactor/compatibility-gates (#1428), console: in-product-banner (#717)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: High-volume customers may experience elevated error rates during automated upgrades -> Mitigation: preflight checks, canary upgrade path, option for manual window
Risk: Confusion from ambiguous messaging -> Mitigation: single unified FAQ, concise in-console copy, translation/localization review
Risk: SDK consumers miss compile-time warnings -> Mitigation: ship package updates with deprecation warnings and CI lint rules that can be surfaced in repos
Risk: Rollback complexity in Dedicated environments -> Mitigation: document exact data/behavior compatibility matrix and provide rollback scripts for Eng ops
success_metrics: Upgrade conversion rate >= 60% within first 30 days for self-serve cohort
< 0.5% of migrated customers report P0 regressions attributable to the change
Support volume from affected areas decreases week-over-week during guided migration
notes: This playbook emphasizes a staged compatibility fade rather than an immediate hard-sunset to reduce customer churn.
We should surface a "Schedule Concierge" CTA for accounts exceeding X monthly tokens where the Concierge team will own migration execution.
Investigate adding a migration simulation tool in the Console to show customers the impact of the change against a sample of their recent requests.
Coordinate with Legal for outbound communications templates for customers under contract requiring 90-day notice.
